source.title: FAME: Fictional Actors for Multilingual Erasure
source.authors: Claudio Savelli; Moreno La Quatra; Alkis Koudounas; F. Giobergia

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the reported values can be assigned to models, methods, and metrics.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies several unlearning methods and measures performance on forgotten data and MMLU, bearing on unlearning efficacy and utility. It does not test post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper measures unlearning outcomes, not recovery by fine-tuning after unlearning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks. Its FT method is an unlearning baseline trained on the retain set, not a recovery attack. The reported SBF metric is SacreBLEU, not accuracy, and the paper states no chance-level threshold. No rows are recorded for cited findings from other studies.
record.test_reason: A new benchmark setting (synthetic multilingual fictional-actor QA, Llama-3.2 1B/3B) that reports forget-set SacreBLEU against Original and Gold models, plus MMLU, for five TOFU-style methods. This bears on the first two parts of version A: forgetting to the target and keeping general ability. No recovery attack (fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, prompting) is run, so B–F and A's attack-resistance part are untested. The target here is the Gold retain-only model, not chance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude GA alone is not viable: it collapses the 1B model and barely changes the 3B model. Effective unlearning needs a controlled disruptive signal jointly optimized with a stability term (GD, KLM). PO yields non-informative refusals, but these are a detectable sign the forgotten data was seen. KLM sometimes gives Gold-like incorrect answers, read as successful unlearning. FT preserves utility but largely fails to forget.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates five unlearning methods on synthetic multilingual fictional-actor data, with entity-based and instance-based splits; it does not evaluate the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model size, split, and unlearning method; GA is described as collapsing useful capabilities for 1B and as insufficient for 3B.

fits_no_version.finding: PO gives a distinctive refusal only on forget items. The authors call this a telltale sign the model saw them. MIA stays near Original (e.g., .911 vs .935; Gold .499) for most methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-level unlearning leaves detectable traces (refusal patterns, membership-inference signal) of the forgotten data.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
record.problems: SacreBLEU is not accuracy, and the paper provides no chance-level reference for this measure. Results use synthetic fictional biographies and two Llama instruction-tuned backbones. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: SBR, SBT, MIA, speedup, and qualitative response examples in Tables 2–4 were omitted because they do not directly measure recovery attacks or the targeted-forgetting/general-ability outcomes recorded here. The MIA and speedup columns are in Tables 2–3; SBR and SBT are also in Tables 2–3; examples are in Table 4.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. No near-chance reference; Gold is used instead. Per-language results are not reported despite five languages.
Activation-direction ablation; mechanistic analysis of blocking vs deleting.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, cross-language queries, in-context recovery. Language-wise forgetting is not broken out.
No counter-method is evaluated against attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The rows_left_out reasoning for SBR and MIA is weak. SBR (retain set) is the evidence for the authors' GA-collapse claim, and MIA bears on residual traces; consider adding SBR rows for GA 1B. Several MMLU 'partial' states (r04, r08, r12, r16) are drops of only .01–.025 against a near-chance 1B MMLU (about .25–.28), so MMLU is weakly informative for the 1B model. FT rows (r01, r11, r21, r31) are a baseline method; FT fails on 1B but partly reduces SBF on 3B. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures forgetting and MMLU utility, but does not test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge or establish a chance-level threshold.
Post-unlearning fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples as a recovery attack.
Activation-direction ablation and analysis demonstrating that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Recovery by rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
A counter-method tested for resistance to the listed recovery attacks.

relation.reason: Its results on forgetting versus utility bear on the first part of A. It is a benchmark paper, so the bearing is partial.

tranche.reason: New setting (synthetic multilingual fictional-actor QA) with forget and MMLU results on the first parts of A; no recovery attacks. Not T2, since the methods are the same TOFU-style ones.

source_check.notes: Forget measure is SacreBLEU vs a Gold retain-only model (no chance level), pooled over five languages with no per-language results. MIA stays far from Gold (about .50) for every method except 1B GA. On 3B instance, the FT control (39.5) matches GD/KLM/PO. 1B MMLU is near chance (.277). Single seed, no uncertainty.

statements.correction: FAME, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, entity split, KLM: SBF 79.5 -> 38.1 (Gold 29.2); MMLU .277 -> .256 (Gold .343); SBR 80.5 -> 75.2; MIA .935 -> .844 (Gold .499). No recovery attack; no chance level.
statements.problem: Gives no FAME number (the 8B multilingual figures belong to another cited study). The cited r07 does not reach Gold level: SBF 38.1 vs Gold 29.2, MMLU drops to .256, MIA stays .844 vs Gold .499. No recovery attack run.

statements.correction: GA, entity split: 1B SBF 79.5 -> 34.7, SBR 80.5 -> 36.3, MMLU .277 -> .252 (authors: collapse); 3B SBF 49.2 -> 49.7 (authors: signal insufficient to modify the model). Ascent loss dampened x0.1, one epoch. Both Llama-3.2, so no family contrast.
statements.problem: Names no FAME finding. Cited rows fit a size effect only for GA, within one family (Llama-3.2). r04 is an MMLU row; the matching forget row is r03. 1B and 3B also differ in fine-tuning epochs (5 vs 10) and Original SBF (79.5 vs 49.2).
